extracted.intended_audience: LTCH administrators, hospital finance officers, Medicare policy stakeholders, CMS commentators and legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed CMS rule addendum describing FY2027 updates to the Long-Term Care Hospital (LTCH) Prospective Payment System (PPS), including proposed payment update factors, wage index methodology, labor-related share, COLAs for Alaska/Hawaii, high-cost outlier policy, and budget neutrality calculations. Intended to inform payment calculations and solicit public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual update factor to LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to apply an update factor of 1.024 to the FY 2026 LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate of $50,824.51 to determine the proposed FY 2027 LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also propose to reduce the annual update by 2.0 percentage points for LTCHs that fail to submit required quality reporting data under the LTCH QRP, resulting in an update factor of 1.004 (0.4 percent) for those LTCHs. The proposed update reflects a proposed annual market basket update of 3.2 percent reduced by a proposed 0.8 percentage point productivity adjustment (section 1886(m)(3)(A)(i)), minus 2.0 percentage points for failure to submit LTCH QRP data (section 1886(m)(5)). Example calculations are provided (e.g., $50,824.51 × 1.024 × budget neutrality factor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Area wage level budget neutrality factor (application and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with §412.523(d)(4), apply an area wage level budget neutrality factor (proposed 1.0025505) to the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate to ensure proposed changes to the area wage level adjustment (including wage index updates, 5-percent cap on decreases, and labor-related share) are budget neutral and do not change estimated aggregate LTCH PPS payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology for calculating the factor is described (see separate budget neutrality methodology entries). The factor is applied multiplicatively to the standard Federal payment rate (example shown: 1.0025505). The factor is based on best available data (e.g., FY2025 MedPAR claims) and includes application of the 5-percent cap in its determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic classifications (labor market areas) for LTCH PPS wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply LTCH PPS area wage level adjustment based on geographic classification (labor market area) where the LTCH is located: either an 'urban area' or a 'rural area' as defined in §412.503 (urban = Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) including Metropolitan division; rural = any area outside urban).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027, propose to continue using CBSA-based labor market area delineations established in OMB Bulletin No. 23-01 (2020 Standards), adopted in the FY2025 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule. Proposed FY2027 wage index tables (Table 12A urban, 12B rural) are provided in Addendum VI and on CMS website. CBSAs are composed of constituent counties; FIPS county codes will continue to be used for county-to-CBSA crosswalks (link to CMS files). Historical references to prior final rules provided for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FIPS county codes for county-to-CBSA crosswalk
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY2027, continue using the Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) county codes, maintained by the U.S. Census Bureau, for purposes of crosswalking counties to CBSAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current county-to-CBSA crosswalk was adopted under the LTCH PPS in the FY2025 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule and is located on the CMS website at the specified 'other-files-download' location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor-related share composition and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose that the LTCH PPS labor-related share for FY2027 is the sum of the FY2027 relative importance of each labor-related cost category in the 2022-based LTCH market basket plus a portion of the capital-related cost relative importance (the portion influenced by local labor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, include Wages and Salaries; Employee Benefits; Professional Fees: Labor-Related; Administrative and Facilities Support Services; Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Services; All Other: Labor-Related Services (sum = 69.1% based on IHS Global Inc. Q4 2025 forecast). Capital-related costs' labor-influenced portion assumed 46% of capital relative importance; with capital relative importance 8.4%, 46% yields 3.9%. Therefore proposed total labor-related share = 73.0%. CMS proposes to use more recent data if available between proposed and final rule publication, if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index data sources and computation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to compute FY2027 LTCH PPS area wage index values using the same data used to compute the proposed FY2027 acute care hospital inpatient wage index: wage data collected from cost reports submitted by IPPS hospitals for cost reporting periods beginning during FY2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with historical practice: (1) compute wage index from acute care IPPS hospital wage data without regard to geographic reclassification under sections 1886(d)(8) and (d)(10); (2) apportion multicampus hospital wage data to each CBSA where campuses are located; (3) employ policy for areas with no IPPS wage data (see separate entry). CMS states these are the most recent complete data available and will continue historical methodologies unless data warrant change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for areas with no IPPS wage data
rubrics_metrics.description: For urban CBSAs with no IPPS wage data, determine LTCH PPS wage index value by using an average of all of the urban areas within the State. For rural areas with no IPPS wage data, determine the wage index value by using the unweighted average of the wage indices from all CBSAs contiguous to the rural counties of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: Hinesville, GA (CBSA 25980) determined as the average of other urban areas within Georgia; rural North Dakota (CBSA 35) determined by averaging contiguous proposed CBSAs. CMS notes number of areas without IPPS wage data may vary over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent 5-percent cap on LTCH PPS wage index decreases
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy finalized to apply a permanent 5-percent cap on any decrease to an LTCH's wage index from its wage index in the prior year; an LTCH's wage index will not be less than 95 percent of its wage index for the prior fiscal year (reflected at §412.525(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cap adjustment is determined based on the wage index value applicable to the LTCH on the last day of the prior Federal fiscal year. Newly opened LTCHs operational on/after the first day of the fiscal year are not subject to the wage index cap and receive the calculated area wage index. The cap is included in the area wage level budget neutrality factor. CMS will publish, in a supplemental data file, each LTCH's prior year final wage index, uncapped current year wage index, and capped current year wage index; newly opened LTCHs may need to contact their MAC due to data lag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent 5-percent cap on decreases in applicable IPPS comparable wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy finalized to apply a permanent 5-percent cap on decreases in an LTCH's applicable IPPS comparable wage index from its applicable IPPS comparable wage index in the prior year (reflected at §412.529(d)(4)(ii)(B) and (d)(4)(iii)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cap applies when calculating IPPS comparable amounts/equivalent amounts required for short-stay-outlier, site neutral, and other adjustments. Unlike the LTCH PPS wage index cap, changes to the applicable IPPS comparable wage index are not budget neutralized; the cap on decreases is not applied in a budget neutral manner. Newly opened LTCHs are not subject to the cap in their first year (same operational-date exception). Supplemental data file will include values used in determining capped applicable IPPS comparable wage indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental wage index data file publication
rubrics_metrics.description: For each LTCH identified in rulemaking data, CMS will include in a supplemental public data file the wage index values from both fiscal years used in determining its capped wage index: the LTCH's final prior year wage index, uncapped current year wage index, and capped current year wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File will be posted on the CMS website (link provided). Due to lags in rulemaking data, a newly opened LTCH may not be listed for a few years and may contact their MAC to ensure correct wage index application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for area wage level adjustment budget neutrality calculation (steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.523(d)(4), determine an area wage level adjustment budget neutrality factor to be applied to the standard Federal payment rate such that estimated aggregate LTCH PPS payments are unaffected by updates to area wage index values or labor-related share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes a four-step methodology for FY2027: Step 1 — simulate aggregate payments using FY2026 wage index values and FY2026 labor-related share (72.9%); Step 2 — simulate aggregate payments using proposed FY2027 wage index values (including 5% cap) and proposed FY2027 labor-related share (73.0%); Step 3 — calculate the ratio (FY2026 simulated total / FY2027 simulated total) to determine the budget neutrality factor; Step 4 — apply the factor to determine the FY2027 standard Federal payment rate after annual update. CMS proposes to use most recent data available, including FY2025 MedPAR claims, and to include only claims that qualified for payment at the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate under the dual rate LTCH PPS in these simulations. Using this methodology, CMS determined a proposed factor of 1.0025505 for FY2027 and applied it in calculating proposed rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) methodology for LTCHs in Alaska and Hawaii (prior and proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.525(b), provide a COLA for LTCHs located in Alaska and Hawaii by multiplying the nonlabor-related portion of the standard Federal payment rate by applicable COLA factors established annually by CMS. Historically used OPM COLA factors updated by CPI comparisons; for FY2027 propose to use DOD Overseas Cost-of-Living Allowance (OCOLA) data effective January 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical approach: updated 2009 OPM COLA factors using CPI for Urban Alaska/Hawaii vs. average U.S. city CPI, reweighted to IPPS market basket nonlabor composition, and applied a 25% cap (statutorily embedded in OPM factors). Proposed approach: use DOD OCOLAs (reflect price differences including shipping, based on Living Pattern Survey and prices for ~150 goods/services) available for 26 Alaska and 6 Hawaii locality areas; use OPM-designated Nonforeign COLA Areas (4 for Alaska, 4 for Hawaii). Where multiple DOD OCOLAs exist within a 50-mile radius of an OPM city, average the local OCOLAs (examples: Anchorage average of Anchorage and Wasilla localities; Fairbanks average of College, Eielson AFB, Fairbanks localities; Rest of Alaska average of Bethel and Kenai). For Maui/Kalawao average Maui and Molokai locality OCOLAs. CMS proposes to eliminate the prior 25% cap starting FY2027. CMS solicits comments on use of DOD OCOLAs, potential impacts (e.g., Service member commissary discounts), possible phase-in or transition approaches, and will continue to update COLAs when labor-related share of IPPS market basket is updated in future years.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-Cost Outlier (HCO) policy for LTCH PPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain HCO adjustment to account for cases with extraordinarily high costs: additional payments are made based on the degree to which estimated cost of a case (Medicare allowable covered charge × hospital CCR) exceeds a fixed-loss amount. LTCH receives 80 percent of the difference between estimated cost and applicable HCO threshold (sum of LTCH PPS payment and applicable fixed-loss amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under dual-rate LTCH PPS: LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate cases retain historic 8-percent HCO target and have a fixed-loss amount calculated using only data from cases that would have been paid at the standard Federal rate. Site neutral payment rate cases adopt the IPPS operating HCO target (currently 5.1%) and use the IPPS fixed-loss amount. To maintain budget neutrality, a budget neutrality requirement and factor is applied to LTCH PPS payments for site neutral payment rate cases; further details and references to prior final rules provided.
